why: Kahn's algorithm run layer by layer: the steps with in-degree 0 form stage 0, removing them exposes stage 1, and so on. Each step lands in the earliest stage its prerequisites allow, which is its longest-path depth in the DAG.
hints: Which steps can run at the very start? Once they are all done, which steps become free?
Process Kahn's algorithm one whole frontier at a time instead of one node at a time. Each frontier is a stage.

Map names to successor sets (deduplicating repeated pairs) and in-degrees; frontier = sorted names with in-degree 0; build the next frontier from successors that drop to 0; sort each stage. O((V + E) log V).
pitfalls: Repeated identical pairs must count once, or in-degrees never reach 0.
Names can contain spaces and mixed case; sort by plain string order.
